title: JWST Detection of Methane on Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS
author: JWST Collaboration / Multiple Teams

layer_assignment.confidence_rationale: JWST mid-infrared spectroscopy is a validated technique. Methane detection in cometary atmospheres follows established spectroscopic methods. 3I/ATLAS is a confirmed hyperbolic-orbit interstellar object.

key_claims.statement: JWST detected methane (CH4) in the coma of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS via mid-infrared spectroscopy.
key_claims.empirical_status: JWST observation; methane spectral features confirmed

key_claims.statement: This is the first chemical fingerprint of an interstellar object, providing compositional data on material that formed around another star.
key_claims.empirical_status: Confirmed; previous interstellar objects (1I/Oumuamua, 2I/Borisov) had no comparable spectroscopic characterization

key_claims.statement: The methane detection constrains the thermal history and formation environment of the object's parent system.

cross_references.relation: User's 2023 'statistical alien lens' scoring of 3I/ATLAS at 7/10 (70%) artificial probability; JWST methane data provides empirical update for revised scoring
Loeb chirality framework: if 3I/ATLAS or future interstellar objects yield biological material, chirality analysis is the first diagnostic
Sgr A* wind cavity (COSMO-003) and 3I/ATLAS both represent quiescent-state structure detection in different astrophysical contexts

pattern_resonance.description: First-contact observation principle: when encountering an unknown system (interstellar object, dark matter halo, alien signal), the minimal informative measurement is spectroscopic/compositional. 3I/ATLAS methane is the astrophysical analog of A_c's minimal-observable approach.

actionable_insights: Update 3I/ATLAS artificial probability score using new compositional data (methane presence argues for natural cometary origin, lowering artificial probability)
